Total EU GHG emissions (European Climate Law scope)  (Mt CO₂eq)

What it measures: ESABCC progress indicator O1. Total EU-27 GHG emissions in the scope of the European Climate Law (EU-27 plus international aviation and maritime). 2030 target: -55% vs 1990; 2050: climate neutrality; ESABCC 2040 advice range: -90 to -95%.

How it's calculated:
  1. Each component is first built from the detailed source rows (combined and unit-scaled as needed).
  2. Add up International aviation, Energy supply, Industry, Transport, Buildings and agriculture energy, Agriculture, LULUCF, Waste and other sectors, and International maritime.

Why it's done this way:
  This is an accounting identity: the source reports these categories as mutually exclusive and exhaustive, so their sum is the total by construction — no modelling assumption is introduced, only disaggregated official data are re-aggregated.

⚠ Caveat:
  International maritime is included at a fixed scope factor (≈0.64) — confirm it matches the intended European Climate Law attribution. 'Waste and other sectors' is a residual (total net emissions minus the listed sectors), so it absorbs any unlisted items.

The columns in this sheet (and why each is needed):
  • Value — the final number plotted on the website, in Mt CO₂eq.
  • International aviation — intermediate step, computed as 1.D.1.a - International Aviation ÷ 1000. It prepares this component from the detailed source rows so the final line can combine them.
  • Energy supply — intermediate step, computed as (1.A.1 - Energy Industries + 1.B - Fugitive Emissions from Fuels) ÷ 1000. It prepares this component from the detailed source rows so the final line can combine them.
  • Industry — intermediate step, computed as (1.A.2 - Manufacturing Industries and Construction + 2 - Industrial Processes and Product Use) ÷ 1000. It prepares this component from the detailed source rows so the final line can combine them.
  • Transport — intermediate step, computed as (1.A.3 - Transport) ÷ 1000. It prepares this component from the detailed source rows so the final line can combine them.
  • Buildings and agriculture energy — intermediate step, computed as 1.A.4 - Other Sectors ÷ 1000. It prepares this component from the detailed source rows so the final line can combine them.
  • Agriculture — intermediate step, computed as 3 - Agriculture ÷ 1000. It prepares this component from the detailed source rows so the final line can combine them.
  • LULUCF — intermediate step, computed as 4 - Land Use, Land - Use Change and Forestry ÷ 1000. It prepares this component from the detailed source rows so the final line can combine them.
  • Waste and other sectors — intermediate step, computed as Total net emissions ÷ 1000 - LULUCF - Agriculture - Buildings and agriculture energy - Transport - Industry - Energy supply. It prepares this component from the detailed source rows so the final line can combine them.
  • International maritime — intermediate step, computed as 1.D.1.b - International Navigation ÷ 1000. It prepares this component from the detailed source rows so the final line can combine them.
  • 1.D.1.a - International Aviation — raw input from EEA GHG data viewer. It is one of the source categories that are added together to form the total, so it has to be captured to reproduce the figure.
  • 1.A.1 - Energy Industries — raw input from EEA GHG data viewer. It is one of the source categories that are added together to form the total, so it has to be captured to reproduce the figure.
  • 1.B - Fugitive Emissions from Fuels — raw input from EEA GHG data viewer. It is one of the source categories that are added together to form the total, so it has to be captured to reproduce the figure.
  • 1.A.2 - Manufacturing Industries and Construction — raw input from EEA GHG data viewer. It is one of the source categories that are added together to form the total, so it has to be captured to reproduce the figure.
  • 2 - Industrial Processes and Product Use — raw input from EEA GHG data viewer. It is one of the source categories that are added together to form the total, so it has to be captured to reproduce the figure.
  • 1.A.3 - Transport — raw input from EEA GHG data viewer. It is one of the source categories that are added together to form the total, so it has to be captured to reproduce the figure.
  • 1.A.4 - Other Sectors — raw input from EEA GHG data viewer. It is one of the source categories that are added together to form the total, so it has to be captured to reproduce the figure.
  • 3 - Agriculture — raw input from EEA GHG data viewer. It is one of the source categories that are added together to form the total, so it has to be captured to reproduce the figure.
  • 4 - Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry — raw input from EEA GHG data viewer. It is one of the source categories that are added together to form the total, so it has to be captured to reproduce the figure.
  • Total net emissions — raw input from EEA GHG data viewer. It is one of the source categories that are added together to form the total, so it has to be captured to reproduce the figure.
  • 1.D.1.b - International Navigation — raw input from EEA GHG data viewer. It is one of the source categories that are added together to form the total, so it has to be captured to reproduce the figure.

Formula:
  Value = (International aviation + Energy supply + Industry + Transport + Buildings and agriculture energy + Agriculture + LULUCF + Waste and other sectors) + International maritime × (0.6375)
  International aviation = 1.D.1.a - International Aviation ÷ 1000
  Energy supply = (1.A.1 - Energy Industries + 1.B - Fugitive Emissions from Fuels) ÷ 1000
  Industry = (1.A.2 - Manufacturing Industries and Construction + 2 - Industrial Processes and Product Use) ÷ 1000
  Transport = (1.A.3 - Transport) ÷ 1000
  Buildings and agriculture energy = 1.A.4 - Other Sectors ÷ 1000
  Agriculture = 3 - Agriculture ÷ 1000
  LULUCF = 4 - Land Use, Land - Use Change and Forestry ÷ 1000
  Waste and other sectors = Total net emissions ÷ 1000 - LULUCF - Agriculture - Buildings and agriculture energy - Transport - Industry - Energy supply
  International maritime = 1.D.1.b - International Navigation ÷ 1000

  1. Subtract 2 - Industrial Processes and Product Use from the first (then rescaled to Mt CO₂eq).

Why it's done this way:
  The indicator is the net difference between these two quantities.

How it's calculated:
  1. Add up Power and heat, Petroleum refineries, Other, Fugitive emissions, and Total.

Primary energy consumption (EU-27)  (TWh)

What it measures: ESABCC progress indicator O2 (primary energy component). EED 2030 indicative benchmark applies; Climate Target Plan MIX 2050 trajectory used as longer-run benchmark.

How it's calculated:
  1. Take the raw PEC, reported in Mtoe.
  2. Convert it from Mtoe to TWh.

Why it's done this way:
  A unit conversion is an exact linear rescaling (e.g. 1 toe ≡ 11.63 MWh): it expresses the source's Mtoe data in TWh without changing the underlying physical quantity or introducing any assumption.

The columns in this sheet (and why each is needed):
  • Value — the final number plotted on the website, in TWh.
  • PEC — raw input from Eurostat (nrg_bal_c). This is the published series the indicator reports; no further breakdown is available in the source.
  • Mtoe → TWh — unit-conversion factor (Mtoe → TWh). Needed because the source reports Mtoe but the indicator is shown in TWh; multiplying by it only changes the unit, not the underlying quantity.

Formula:
  Value = PEC × Mtoe → TWh
